mission_phase: Generation 34 - Browser-driven search evaluation (Home Depot, embedded SearchModel)
phase_goal: Evaluate a site's search purely through the real browser (no external API calls, no token replay, no crawling) by reading the search response the page itself receives — for Home Depot, the embedded Apollo SearchModel (totalProducts, correctedKeyword, searchRedirect, semanticToken) plus the rendered product titles. Run a targeted query set designed to surface failures: dimension/unit queries (1/2 in vs 1/2 ft, #2 bit), synonym consistency (drywall sheets / sheetrock / sheet rock), and pro/trade names (romex, unistrut). Record each query as a debuggable experiment (exact search URL + observed result + top titles).
reason_generation_started: Operator: build the browser-driven search evaluation and try tricky queries (dimensions like 1/2 in vs 1/2 ft, # sizes, drywall synonym consistency, pro queries) to see if Home Depot's search brings noise / inconsistency — the kind of big failure we saw with 'sofa' on a Woo site.
standing_directive: Read only what the real browser legitimately receives (embedded SearchModel + rendered DOM) for a bounded, user-requested query set — equivalent to a person running those searches. Do NOT call apionline.homedepot.com from a scraper, do NOT replay Akamai/session tokens, do NOT crawl beyond the query set. Report observed evidence; never fabricate a result count or title.

functional: For each query the evaluation records: the exact search URL, whether it stayed on search (/s/) or redirected to a category (/b/), totalProducts, correctedKeyword (spell handling), and the top rendered product titles.

Dimension queries are assessed for noise (do the top titles match the requested size/unit); the drywall synonym trio is compared for consistency (similar totalProducts / same redirect); pro/trade names are checked for correct mapping.
Every reported number/claim ties back to the exact query URL and the observed on-page evidence (debuggable).
usability: Findings clearly separate PASS (intent handled) from failures (noise / synonym inconsistency), with the evidence per query.
No crawling beyond the bounded query set; no external API calls.
technical: Results are captured to an honest artifact (JSON) under the Home Depot assessment dir; if surfaced in the dashboard it reuses the debuggable/navigable report pattern; existing gate stays green; git diff --check clean.

validation_notes: VAL-083: 15 queries via browser; findings HD-F001/002/003; passes for pro/intent/spelled-fraction; artifact + report written; no code changed.
known_gaps_opened: A dashboard view for browser-driven (non-Shopify/Woo) search evaluations is not built; results live as an artifact + markdown report.
Result counts for category-redirect queries reflect the redirected category page, not a raw search total — noted in findings.
